title: Brazilian Benefit-Card Transactions (Synthetic)
subtitle: 5.7M benefit-card purchases answered by a simulated issuer, with fraud labels
description:
## Context

In Brazil, employers give employees benefit cards — meal (*refeição*), food (*alimentação*), mobility, multi-benefit, incentive — whose balances can only be spent on certain things. A card belongs to a **program** that fixes its **wallets** (one balance each) and its network: the issuer's **proprietary network**, where the shop's CNAE (economic activity code) decides which wallet it accepts, or a **brand** (Visa, Mastercard, Elo), where the MCC decides. Each wallet is credited every month and spent until it runs out.

Real transaction data from this market isn't public. This dataset is **synthetic**: no row is real. But every row went through what a real one goes through — a simulated issuer checks the card, the cardholder, the shop, the terminal, the PIN, which wallet the shop accepts and whether there is balance, then approves or declines with an ISO 8583 response code and a specific reason. The result behaves like the market: relationships that hold, distributions that look right, business rules followed everywhere.

## Content

One simulated year, **September 2025 to August 2026**, as a star schema in Parquet:

| File | Rows | What it holds |
|---|---:|---|
| `fact_transactions.parquet` | 5,689,874 | Every purchase, withdrawal or reversal attempt and the issuer's answer |
| `fact_balance_movements.parquet` | 5,608,434 | The ledger: monthly credits, debits and reversals, chained per wallet |
| `dim_card_wallets.parquet` | 79,517 | Each wallet of each card: monthly credit, limits, final balance |
| `dim_cards.parquet` | 45,847 | Cards: program, network, physical or virtual |
| `dim_cardholders.parquet` | 34,432 | Employees: employer, municipality, admission |
| `dim_companies.parquet` | 800 | Employers by segment (SME, Middle, Corporate, Public) and their branches |
| `dim_establishments.parquet` | 8,000 | Shops, online businesses and cash machines: category, CNAE, MCC, municipality |
| `dim_terminals.parquet` | 12,000 | POS, TEF, e-commerce gateways and ATMs, with their acquirer |
| `dim_wallets`, `dim_card_programs`, `dim_transaction_modalities`, `dim_acquirers` | small | The catalogues |
| `ref_response_codes`, `ref_program_wallets`, `ref_cnae_wallets`, `ref_mcc_wallets`, `ref_mcc_modalities` | small | The rules behind each answer: codes, which wallets a program holds, which wallet a CNAE or MCC accepts, which brand accepts an MCC |

Also included: `data_dictionary.md` (every column described), `quality_report.md` (the checks the data passed) and `dataset_metadata.json` (seed, window, code version, row counts).

Key columns of `fact_transactions`: `amount` (BRL), `date`, `response_code` (`00` = approved), `decline_reason` (e.g. `insufficient_balance`, `wallet_not_accepted_at_cnae`, `wrong_pin`), `wallet_id` (the wallet the issuer charged), `capture_type`, `is_fraud`, `fraud_scenario` and `disputed`. The ids join every table; there is no CPF, CNPJ, card number or person name.

## What the data looks like

- **85–90% approved each month**, varying with no trend; about half the declines are for lack of balance.
- **Spending follows the credit:** most cardholders spend their whole monthly benefit, a few let it build up; the credit lands on the 1st and spending jumps that day.
- **Time:** restaurants peak at lunch and dip on weekends, supermarkets peak on Saturday, fuel before and after work; national holidays, Christmas Eve and Black Friday move the volume; one company in three gives a year-end credit in December.
- **Place:** real IBGE municipalities; companies where the economy is, shops where people live; most in-person purchases in the cardholder's state.
- **Fraud (~0.5%)** labelled by scenario — mobile wallet after an account takeover, card not present, card intercepted before delivery, skimming at a point of compromise — and **disputes**, including legit purchases contested by mistake: `is_fraud` is the truth, `disputed` is what an issuer would see.

## How it was made

An open-source pipeline (Python, Polars, PostgreSQL, DuckDB) generates the world, simulates the attempts month by month in time order — balances move, daily limits count, reversals come later — and exports only if 83 quality checks and a statistical profile pass. The same seed reproduces the same dataset: [github.com/Nic-Soares/corporate-benefits-transactions](https://github.com/Nic-Soares/corporate-benefits-transactions).

The reference data is public — IBGE (CNAE, municipalities, population, municipal GDP) and the public MCC list. Every weight, balance, limit, ticket and acceptance rule is synthetic, shaped after how the Brazilian benefits market works, not taken from any company's data.

## Limitations

- **Synthetic rates.** Approval, decline mix, tickets and fraud share have a realistic shape but are not statistics of the real market; don't draw conclusions about it from them.
- **Snapshot dimensions.** Each record carries its current status and the day it began (`status_since`; active before that day), not a full history of changes.
- **One fact for attempts and reversals.** Reversals are rows of `fact_transactions` with `transaction_type = 'reversal'`, pointing to the purchase they undo; filter them out for attempt-level rates.
- **Simplified world.** Acceptance rules, fraud scenarios and the calendar follow how the market works in broad strokes; acquirer integrations, chargebacks, fees and settlement are out of scope.

## Ideas

- Predict declines (and which reason) from the attempt alone
- Fraud detection with label noise: train on `disputed`, evaluate on `is_fraud`
- Spending and seasonality by category, segment or state
- Data engineering: incremental loads, slowly changing dimensions (`status_since`), ledger reconciliation, dashboards

resources.description: Every attempt to pay, withdraw or reverse with a benefit card, and the issuer's answer. One row per attempt.

fields.name: related_transaction_id
fields.description: For a reversal, the purchase it undoes

fields.name: modality_id
fields.description: Network the card runs on: OWN (issuer's proprietary network, 3-party) or VISA, MASTERCARD, ELO (4-party)

fields.name: card_wallet_id
fields.description: Wallet of the card the issuer charged (dim_card_wallets); on a decline for balance, the wallet it would have charged; empty when the decline came before a wallet was chosen

fields.name: wallet_id
fields.description: Type of that wallet: FOOD, MEAL, MOBILITY, HEALTH, HOME_OFFICE, EDUCATION, GIFT, PREMIUM

fields.name: transaction_type
fields.description: purchase, withdrawal (cash, brand cards, GIFT wallet) or reversal

fields.name: wallet_option
fields.description: Proprietary network: the option picked on the terminal (FOOD, MEAL, OTHERS); empty on brand cards

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date and time of the attempt; volume follows the week, the month, national holidays and their eves, Christmas, New Year's Eve and Black Friday

fields.name: capture_type
fields.description: How the card was read: CHIP, MAG_STRIPE, CONTACTLESS, MOBILE_NFC, APPLE_PAY, GOOGLE_PAY, ECOMMERCE

fields.name: pin_status
fields.description: ok, wrong or not_required (contactless, wallets, online)

fields.name: decline_reason
fields.description: Specific cause of a decline (one ISO code covers several); empty when approved

fields.name: nsu
fields.description: Sequence number the terminal gave the attempt

fields.name: authorization_code
fields.description: Issuer's authorization code; empty when declined

fields.name: is_fraud
fields.description: Ground truth: made by someone other than the cardholder

fields.name: fraud_scenario
fields.description: How the fraud happened: account_takeover_wallet, card_not_present, intercepted_card, point_of_compromise; empty when not fraud

fields.name: disputed
fields.description: The cardholder contested it; true for most approved fraud and for a few legit purchases contested by mistake

resources.description: Every change of a wallet's balance: the monthly credit, debits of approved purchases and withdrawals, reversals. One row per movement.

fields.name: transaction_id
fields.description: Transaction that moved it (fact_transactions); empty for the monthly credit

fields.name: operation_type
fields.description: credit (the monthly benefit; the first, pro rata, on activation; a year-end extra some employers give on 10 December), purchase, withdrawal or reversal

fields.name: operation_amount
fields.description: Amount moved in BRL, always positive

fields.name: operation_date
fields.description: Date and time of the movement

fields.name: sequence_number
fields.description: Order of the movements, 1 = first; breaks ties of movements at the same second

resources.description: Each wallet a card holds, with its monthly credit and limits. The employer picks, per program, which of the program's wallets (ref_program_wallets) its employees get.

fields.name: monthly_credit
fields.description: Benefit credited on the 1st of each month, BRL; a wallet activated in the period first gets a share of it, pro rata to the days left in that month, on the activation day

fields.name: daily_limit
fields.description: Most that can be spent per day, BRL; 0 = no limit

fields.name: monthly_limit
fields.description: Most that can be spent per month, BRL; 0 = no limit

fields.name: daily_count_limit
fields.description: Most approved purchases per day; 0 = no limit

fields.name: final_balance
fields.description: Balance at the end of the simulated period

fields.name: activation_date
fields.description: Date the wallet was activated, a few days after the card's issue

fields.name: status_since
fields.description: Date the current status began; the wallet was active before it

resources.description: Benefit cards. The program fixes the wallets and the network.

fields.name: expiration_date
fields.description: Last day of the current plastic; a card is renewed on expiry and keeps its id

fields.name: issue_date
fields.description: Date first issued, a few days after the cardholder's admission

fields.name: status
fields.description: active, inactive (not unlocked yet), blocked or cancelled

fields.name: status_since
fields.description: Date the current status began; the card was active before it (an inactive card never was: since its issue)

resources.description: Employees who hold the cards. No names or documents.

fields.name: status_since

resources.description: Employers that give the benefits. Holdings and their branches. No CNPJ.

fields.name: parent_id
fields.description: Holding of a branch; empty for a holding

fields.name: segment
fields.description: Size of the employer: SME (1-250 employees), Middle (251-1,999), Corporate (2,000+) or Public (government). The dataset holds a sample of each company's cardholders, not its whole headcount

resources.description: Shops, online businesses and cash machines where cards are used. No CNPJ.

fields.name: mcc_code

fields.name: status_since

resources.description: Wallet types: what each balance can be spent on.
Card programs: the wallets a card holds and the network it runs on.
Networks: the issuer's proprietary network and the card brands.
Acquirers that run the terminals, and the ATM network.
ISO 8583 response codes used in the dataset.
Wallets each card program allows. A multi-benefit card holds the ones its employer picked out of these.

fields.description: CNAE prefix (class, 4 digits, or subclass, 7 digits)
